steps: A regular 6-gon maps onto itself when a vertex moves to the position of another vertex.
The vertices are spaced 360 ÷ 6 = 60° apart, so that is the smallest rotation that works.
Multiples of 60° also work, and there are 6 of them in a full turn.
Excluding the 360° rotation, which is the identity, leaves 5 rotations strictly between 0° and 360°.

steps: Both vertices had every coordinate negated: (8, 4) → (-8, -4) and (4, -8) → (-4, 8).
A single reflection across an axis changes exactly one coordinate's sign, and it reverses orientation sense, so no reflection fits.
A translation adds the same fixed vector to every point. Here A moved by ⟨-16, -8⟩ but B moved by ⟨-8, 16⟩, and those differ, so it is not a translation.
Negating both coordinates of every point while preserving orientation is exactly a 180° rotation about the origin.
